source_corrections.evidence: the resulting cumulative wrapper passes pinned PreTeXt validation and preserves the prompt-definition-prompt reading sequence
source_corrections.source_issue: a semantic definition is nested inside a task statement and violates the pinned PreTeXt content model
source_corrections.target_action: split the exploration at that point and place the unchanged definition at section level while preserving its exact reading order index and mathematics

source_corrections.evidence: the defining union and all subsequent uses already range over O_A
source_corrections.source_issue: openness of O_A supplies a ball only for each a in O_A rather than for every a in A
source_corrections.target_action: replace the quantified set A with O_A

source_corrections.evidence: B_A(a,delta)=B_X(a,delta) intersection A is contained in O_X intersection A=O_A
source_corrections.source_issue: the reverse-implication activity asks for a ball in A contained in A which is automatic and does not prove openness
source_corrections.target_action: ask for the natural ball B_A(a,delta) contained in O_A

source_corrections.evidence: the paired factor is X_2 and all displayed domains and coordinates use X_1 times X_2
source_corrections.source_issue: the first factor is introduced twice as (X,d_1) although every product and coordinate uses X_1
source_corrections.target_action: replace X with X_1 in both factor declarations

source_corrections.source_issue: the triangle proof falsely drops a positive cross term and asserts d(x,z)^2 is at most d(x,y)^2+d(y,z)^2
source_corrections.target_action: apply Cauchy-Schwarz to bound the cross term and obtain d(x,z)^2 at most (d(x,y)+d(y,z))^2 before taking square roots

source_corrections.evidence: their Cartesian product is then the intended rectangle in R squared
source_corrections.source_issue: the real intervals [1,2] and [3,4] are called subspaces of R squared without an embedding

source_corrections.evidence: the displayed sum and product are finite and indexed by a positive integer n
source_corrections.source_issue: any number overclaims the displayed unweighted Euclidean construction while the following definition quantifies only i=1 through n
source_corrections.target_action: state any finite number of metric spaces

source_corrections.evidence: this matches thm_relatively_open_ms in the same chapter
source_corrections.source_issue: the relative-open summary writes O_A=X intersection O which collapses to O
source_corrections.target_action: replace X with the subspace A

source_corrections.evidence: the subsequent ambient-closed intersection characterization remains correct
source_corrections.source_issue: the first closed-set characterization writes C_A=A intersection O_A for open O_A and therefore describes an open set
source_corrections.target_action: restore the definition C_A=A setminus O_A

source_corrections.evidence: the chapter and exercise use the Euclidean metric and metric-subspace definition
source_corrections.source_issue: the pair (R,d_E) is called a topological space although d_E is a metric rather than a topology
source_corrections.target_action: replace topological space with metric space

source_corrections.evidence: the displayed rule has ordered-pair arguments (x_1,y_1) and (x_2,y_2)
source_corrections.source_issue: the sum-distance rule takes two points of X times Y but its declared function domain contains only one product point
source_corrections.target_action: declare d from (X times Y) times (X times Y) to R

source_corrections.evidence: the displayed rule evaluates d(x,y) for two elements x and y of that finite product
source_corrections.source_issue: the finite-product metric has only the point space as its function domain and then refers to undefined X
source_corrections.target_action: define X as the finite product and declare d from X times X to R

source_corrections.evidence: f((x_n)) and f((y_n)) are defined only when both sequences lie in E^m
source_corrections.source_issue: the function f is declared only on E^m but the asserted distance identity quantifies arbitrary elements of H
source_corrections.target_action: replace H with E^m in that quantifier

source_corrections.evidence: each displayed rule has two ordered-pair arguments
source_corrections.source_issue: both true-false product-distance functions take two product points but are declared only on X times Y
source_corrections.target_action: declare each function from (X times Y) times (X times Y) to R

source_corrections.evidence: the chapter definition declares a subspace metric by restricting d to A times A
source_corrections.source_issue: the subspace metric is abbreviated as d restricted to O although its two-variable domain is O times O
source_corrections.target_action: write the restricted metric as d restricted to O times O
